messages:
maria: Quick summary — ran the ghostplay sampling run against last week's 24h prod trace and saw a consistent 5–7% increase in p50 token latency after the new kernel-selection heuristic landed. Sharing logs and the harness command below.
jon: ugh, thanks. is this with KV warmup enabled?
kevin: which kernel path got chosen more frequently? single-threaded matmul or fused-attn?
maria: KV warmup was ON (default). Kernel selector chose fused-attn for ~78% of requests at avg seq_len 512.
replay-bot: [run 2456789012] completed. summary: requests=12.4k, avg_seq=487, kv_hits=63%, avg_token_latency=11.8ms (baseline 11.1ms)
sam: can you paste the harness invocation? want to try locally.
maria: sure — 
```
./replay_harness --trace /mnt/traces/prod-2026-03-12.pb --anon-mode cohort --sample-rate 0.05 --kv-warmup=on --kernel-policy new-selector --concurrency 48 --profile=perf.json
```
carol: did you run apples-to-apples vs the old-selector with identical sampling seeds?
maria: yes — used seed=42 for the sampling engine. Old-selector run gave avg_token_latency=11.1ms, p95=29ms. New-selector p95=31ms. p50 regressed by ~6% across runs (3 independent runs).
jon: any change in batching occupancy? new selector might be altering batch shapes.
maria: interesting you asked — batching hist shows slightly fewer 32-token batches and more 16-token ones. mean batch_size dropped from 27.4 -> 24.9. Attached profile: /artifacts/2456789012/perf.json
kevin: that would explain some of the perf. fused-attn can be more efficient at larger batch shapes. If selector favors it at moderate seq lengths but lowers batch occupancy, net effect can be worse.
sam: what about KV cache behavior — hit rate dropped?
maria: kv_hits is stable at 63% same as baseline. But KV access latency in the profile spiked by ~15% for the fused-attn path (maybe due to memory layout).
jon: can you dump a small run with kernel=forced-old and kernel=forced-new with identical concurrency and sampling to rule out non-determinism?
maria: already did quick check: forced-old -> p50=11.0ms, forced-new -> p50=11.9ms. All other flags identical.
carol: any parity/determinism mismatches on outputs? we need to ensure retraces still produce same logits for eval set.
maria: ran parity check on 500 eval queries (anon cohort). All top-1 tokens match, logit deltas negligible (<1e-6) except for 3 samples where softmax order flipped at tail (likely numerical).
kevin: sounds numerical rather than algorithmic. But perf regressions still concerning. Hypothesis: kernel selector uses a cost model that underestimates small-batch fused-attn cost and switches when it shouldn't.
jon: actionable: 1) rollback selector default to old for canary hosts, 2) add a micro-benchmark harness that sweeps batch_size x seq_len x kv_hit and reports per-token cost for both kernels, 3) add a sampling test that preserves batch-shape distribution from prod.
maria: agreed. I can add the micro-bench — will implement sweep script and post results. Also will run targeted runs forcing batch occupancy to match prod distribution.
sam: shout if you need infra (more GPUs) for micro-bench.
carol: also add a determinism flag to harness so we can pin any RNGs and snapshot kernel selection decisions per-request for later auditing.
maria: putting that on the todo. For immediate mitigation I propose: flip selector back to safe-threshold until we tune cost model. Rolling a canary tonight at 22:00 UTC.
kevin: thumbs up. After micro-bench we can adjust selector thresholds and re-run apples-to-apples.
jon: one more ask — include KV access breakdown per kernel in the profiling output (latency hist + percentiles). that will help confirm the memory-layout hypothesis.
maria: will add. I'll post the micro-bench results and a short writeup once I have them (~tomorrow morning). Thanks all :thumbsup:
replay-bot: [action] scheduled rollback of kernel-selector to safe-threshold on canary hosts at 2026-03-18T22:00:00Z
carol: leaving an ops note to watch p50/p95 for the canary window. ping @oncall if anything spikes.
maria: noted.
